cut.note: the sixteen 'filters' are ONE loop with a pluggable update; the update rules decompose into four orthogonal modifications of the LMS gradient (normalisation, error shaping, step adaptation, second-order correction), which is the cut below

organs.mechanism: for each sample k: y = w . x[k]; e = d[k] - y; w += learning_rule(e, x[k]); w_history[k] = w before the update; init_weights draws random or zeros or takes a vector
dw = mu * e * x: the instantaneous gradient of e^2 with a fixed step
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: the base every other rule modifies
organs.failure_landscape: UNKNOWN by run; record: mu too large diverges, too small cannot track

organs.mechanism: mu_eff = mu / (eps + x . x): the step shrinks when the regressor is large so the update's effect on e is bounded independent of input scale; eps guards zero input (GNGD adapts eps itself)

the factor e in dw is replaced by f(e): sign(e) (and sign(x)) for SSLMS/NSSLMS, e^3 for LMF, tanh(lambda e) for LLNCOSH, lambda alpha exp(-lambda |e|^alpha) |e|^(alpha-1) sign(e) for GMCC; each is the gradient of a different loss (absolute, quartic, log-cosh, generalised correntropy)
assumptions: the loss chosen matches the noise (heavy tails favour bounded f; light tails favour steeper f)
organs.source_boundary: the e-dependent factor of each rule

organs.mechanism: Mathews: mu += ro * e * last_e * (last_x . x) -- successive errors of the same sign on correlated inputs mean the step is too small; Benveniste: the same with a filtered gradient direction fi carried across steps (fi = (I - mu x x^T) fi + e x); GNGD adapts the regulariser eps by the same product; all keep (last_e, last_mu, last_x) as state
assumptions: ro small; the correlation is a proxy for misadjustment
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: removes the fixed-mu dilemma the record names

organs.mechanism: R (the running inverse of the input autocorrelation) is updated by the matrix inversion lemma: R = (R - R x x^T R / (mu + x^T R x)) / mu with mu the forgetting factor; dw = R x e -- a second-order (Newton-like) step whose direction whitens the input
assumptions: mu (forgetting) in (0, 1]; R initialised to a scaled identity
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: convergence independent of the input's eigenvalue spread, at n^2 cost

organs.mechanism: keep the last `order` regressors X and targets; e_mem = d_mem - X^T w; dw = mu * X (X^T X + eps I)^-1 e_mem -- the smallest weight change that zeroes the last `order` errors; a separate run/adapt because the memory must be shifted per sample
a memory of recent x and d yields means m_x, m_d; the filter predicts on (x - m_x) and adds m_d; the update is NLMS on the centred data (read from the first lines of the rule only)
turns a scalar sequence into rows of the last n values so the filter above can act as an FIR model (by file name and the record's 'identify a 4-tap FIR plant'; not read)
consumers of w_history: a novelty score per sample from how much the weights moved (error and learning-based novelty detection by name; not read)

pressures.condition: the mapping from regressor to target is unknown and changes over time; each sample arrives once; the estimate must move enough to follow and little enough not to chase noise
pressures.resource_or_constraint: one pass; O(n) or O(n^2) per sample; a step-size constant chosen blind
pressures.failure_condition: divergence (step too large) or lag (step too small) -- the record's failure condition
pressures.world_punishes: a fixed step for a non-stationary plant
pressures.world_rewards: a step that reads the input scale and the recent error correlation
pressures.observable_consequence: tap error vs time across a plant switch (the record's entry point)
pressures.vacuity_condition: a stationary plant with unlimited samples (any small step wins)
pressures.trivial_shortcuts: batch least squares on all data (correct, not online; the world must forbid revisiting)
pressures.cheat_control: a filter told the plant's switch times and true taps must show zero error after each switch; if the world scores it equal to LMS at a mu near the stability bound, tracking is not being measured
pressures.purpose_separated_from_pressure: PURPOSE: system identification, echo cancellation, equalisation

pressures.condition: occasional huge errors (impulsive noise) dominate a squared-error gradient and throw the weights
pressures.resource_or_constraint: no knowledge of which samples are outliers
pressures.world_rewards: bounded error nonlinearities (sign, tanh, correntropy kernels)
pressures.observable_consequence: tap error under Gaussian vs impulsive noise for LMS vs SSLMS/LLNCOSH/GMCC
pressures.trivial_shortcuts: clip the error (a crude f(e); the world should allow it)
pressures.cheat_control: a filter told which samples are impulses and skipping them must beat every f(e); if not, the world's noise is not impulsive

pressures.condition: regressor components are correlated; the error surface is a narrow valley; a first-order step converges at the rate of the smallest eigenvalue
pressures.world_rewards: whitening (RLS) or projection onto recent inputs (AP), paid in compute
pressures.observable_consequence: convergence time vs input eigenvalue spread for LMS vs RLS vs AP
pressures.trivial_shortcuts: pre-whiten offline (needs the statistics the pressure hides)
pressures.cheat_control: a filter given the true autocorrelation must converge in ~n steps; if the world cannot separate it from LMS, the input is white
